subject: BrightWave pilot: implementation playbook and open decisions
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Claire Bennett <claire@brightwavehealth.com>, Marcus O'Neil <marcus.oneil@brightwavehealth.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: BrightWave pilot: implementation playbook and open decisions

Claire / Marcus — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the playbook I promised attached. I focused this on the technical asks we discussed so the pilot can start without surprises.

Key pain you described:
- Inference latency variance in triage pipeline (spikes during peak hours, currently 120ms median but 800ms tail in production).
- Budget constraints: must keep per-request inference cost below $0.003 on average for the pilot.
- Accuracy vs. latency tradeoff for reranking step: need to preserve clinical precision for top-3 suggestions.

Goals for the 6-week pilot:
1) End-to-end throughput target: 200 requests/minute steady with 95th percentile latency < 350ms.
2) Maintain top-3 rerank accuracy delta < 1% vs current baseline.
3) Produce production-ready SDK adapter and acceptance criteria for Redwood Dedicated or VPC deployment.

Open technical decisions we flagged (need your prioritization):
A) Streaming + function-calls vs. batch synchronous calls for the triage step. We recommended streaming + early termination for lower median latency and better user feedback, but this requires SDK hooks (see section below).
B) Quantization profile: we can run an INT8-quantized variant for cost, but we should run a quality evaluation on your prompt set (I asked for 500 representative cases).
C) Caching scope: prefix vs. response-level KV cache. Prefix caching helps for repeated templated prompts but not for individualized notes.

Immediate next steps (owners in brackets):
- BrightWave to share 500 anonymized prompt/response pairs and 30 rerank gold examples (Claire) — due 6/8.
- Redwood to deliver a focused SDK adapter draft with streaming hooks + funcall examples and an integration checklist (Rishi / Sergio) — target 6/9.
- Quick QA run with INT8 profile on 100 cases and a latency profile (Sergio) — deliver 6/11.
- Legal/Procurement intro to talk SLA and data residency if you want Dedicated (Marissa) — Marissa will propose times next week.

Attachments included: implementation_playbook (walkthrough + acceptance criteria), checklist (ops items + firewall rules).

If that all looks right I'll schedule a short technical sync next Wednesday with Sergio to walk the SDK hooks.

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood_inference-implementation_playbook.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)
- brightwave-integration-checklist.xlsx (xlsx, 23KB)
From: Claire Bennett <claire@brightwavehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus O'Neil <marcus.oneil@brightwavehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 16:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightWave pilot: implementation playbook and open decisions

Thanks Rishi — this is great and captures everything. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Data: we'll anonymize and deliver the 500 cases (no PHI) by EOD 6/8. Marcus will own that.
2) On streaming: we like the UX for streaming + funcalls (ability to do progressive reranking), but our infra team is concerned about connection stability (we can't easily hold long-lived sockets in the triage tier). If the SDK supports graceful reconnects and resume we can consider it.
3) For quantization, we want to see the quality delta on the 100-case sanity check before we commit to INT8 for the pilot.

One ask: can Redwood's SDK adapter include a short example of how to instrument token-level cost and map it back to our billing events? That will help our finance team sign off.

We'll look out for the SDK draft. Thanks again to you and Sergio — Claire

Claire Bennett
Director of Product — BrightWave Health
Phone: (415) 555-0123
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Claire Bennett <claire@brightwavehealth.com>, Marcus O'Neil <marcus.oneil@brightwavehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightWave pilot: implementation playbook and open decisions

Claire — great notes. A few technical clarifications and what I'll include in the SDK draft: 

1) Streaming + funcalls implementation notes:
- SDK will expose a "streaming_iterator" for partial tokens and allow user callbacks to surface early top-k candidates.
- We'll add a lightweight resume token so if a socket drops we can re-request remaining tokens and stitch on the client side; reconnect latency will be a factor but we can make the resume window conservative (10s).

2) Batching and latency controls:
- We'll add a per-route batching policy suggestion: keep batch windows under 20ms for latency-sensitive triage; enable adaptive batching during off-peak to reduce cost.
- For your throughput target (200 req/min) we expect 1-2 GPUs in dedicated mode or equivalent hosted autoscale. I'll include a cost estimate.

3) Quantization and rerank quality:
- I'll run INT8 and FP16 back-to-back on 100 cases and produce a small p95 latency + delta-accuracy table. INT8 often reduces latency and cost ~25-35% on modern A100/GB200 stacks but effects vary on rerank ranking margin, so we'll test.

4) Structured outputs + funcalls:
- We'll include a sample using Redwood's Structured Output schema for the triage JSON (fields: urgency, recommended_actions[], highlight_spans[]) and a funcall for downstream EHR write.

I'll attach the SDK adapter draft and a short script to run the INT8 sanity test by Wednesday (6/9). One question for Claire/Marcus: do you have an internal endpoint we can use for smoke tests, or should we spin up a Quickstart sandbox on Redwood Dedicated?

Thanks,
Sergio
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: BrightWave pilot: implementation playbook and open decisions

Claire / Marcus — thanks for the quick reply and the connect on constraints. Two quick confirmations and the proposed schedule: 

- Claire will share anonymized prompts by 6/8 (Marcus) — we will treat them as private and run only the quality/latency tests you authorize.
- Sergio will post the SDK draft + INT8 sanity script by 6/9.
- Marissa will send a calendar invite for Legal/Procurement intro (target 6/10 or 6/11).

Proposed short technical sync: Wed 6/9 09:30 PT (30 min) — Sergio to walk streaming adapter and resume semantics; objective: agree on whether streaming+resume or short-lived synchronous calls is the pilot default. Please confirm availability.

Also: Claire asked about token-level cost instrumentation — action for Sergio: include an example mapping streaming tokens -> cost events and a small dashboard example we can import into BrightWave's BI tool.

If you confirm the 6/9 sync and share the 500 cases we’ll consider the pilot officially scoped and draft a short SOW for signature (Marissa will attach).

Best,
Rishi
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
